caloocan.info: Caloocan is a historic city known as the 'Home of the Katipunan'. It played a crucial role during the Philippine Revolution.

heritage_spots.name: Monumento (Bonifacio Monument)
heritage_spots.info: An iconic 45-foot pylon designed by Guillermo Tolentino commemorating Andres Bonifacio.

heritage_spots.name: San Roque Cathedral
heritage_spots.info: Established in 1815, it served as a spiritual center during the Spanish colonial period.

heritage_spots.name: Tandang Sora Birthplace
heritage_spots.info: The site where Melchora Aquino, the 'Mother of the Katipunan', was born.

caloocan.tips: Visit Monumento at night to see the lighting; it's perfect for photography.
caloocan.directions_template: From {user_loc}, take the LRT-1 to Monumento Station or a jeepney passing through McArthur Highway.

malabon.info: A coastal city rich in heritage houses and 17th-century architecture, often called the 'Venice of the Philippines'.

heritage_spots.name: San Bartolome Church
heritage_spots.info: Built in 1614, this Greco-Roman church is a masterpiece of Spanish colonial engineering.

heritage_spots.name: Raymundo Ancestral House
heritage_spots.info: The oldest documented heritage house in Malabon, built in 1861 with a distinct 'Bahay-na-Bato' style. The Raymundo House, also known as the home of Dr. Raymundo “Medico,” is a classic Bahay na Bato built in 1861 that exemplifies Spanish colonial architecture in Malabon. Its most distinguishing exterior feature is the Hapsburg (two-headed) eagle carved into the adobe gateway, accompanied by the Roman numeral "MDCCCLXI" (1861) and a black metal gate. The structure follows the traditional two-story layout, utilizing solid adobe and concrete for the ground floor and wood for the upper level. Inside, the house remains a well-preserved time capsule of 19th-century Filipino craftsmanship, featuring original Capiz windows, massive tree posts, and flooring made of premium hardwoods like narra, kamagong, and ipil. Many of the home's original furnishings, including the narra dining and sofa sets, have remained in use since the house was first constructed.

heritage_spots.name: Angel Cacnio Art Gallery
heritage_spots.info: Home to the works of a Master Painter; a hub for Malabon's local art scene.

heritage_spots.name: Tullahan River
heritage_spots.info: Situated north of Manila, spans approximately 27.1 kilometers (16.8 mi). It originates from the La Mesa Reservoir in Quezon City, passes through Caloocan, Malabon, Valenzuela, and Navotas, and finally drains into Manila Bay. Several barangays have planted ornamental plants, fruit-bearing trees, and vegetables to beautify the banks of the Tullahan River. The river flows through Barangay Potrero, Tinajeros, Maysilo, Muzon, Catmon, Niugan, Tonsuya, and Longos.

heritage_spots.name: Ten Tee King Shi Ong Hu Temple
heritage_spots.info: A two-story Taoist sanctuary in Malabon that exemplifies traditional Chinese architecture through its "Paifang" style stone arch, featuring brown pillars, a green-tiled roof, and a miniature pagoda flanked by dragons. The temple’s exterior is defined by a balcony supported by red pillars, housing a central incense holder and intricate stone carvings of mythological creatures and plants. Inside, the first floor contains a serene altar with three images of Buddha set against a plain ivory ceiling, while the second floor features a more elaborate, red-and-gold altar accompanied by traditional instruments and Chinese lanterns. Following the classic Ming and Qing dynasty courtyard layout, the temple aligns its divine hall along a main axis to symbolize the Taoist pursuit of happiness, longevity, and immortality.

heritage_spots.name: Immaculate Conception Parish
heritage_spots.info: A prominent example of Spanish colonial architecture, characterized by a symmetrical facade and a central bell tower adorned with intricate stonework and arched windows. Its welcoming patio is home to a large statue of Jesus Christ, a replica of the Immaculate Conception, and lush greenery including a mango tree, creating a serene transition from the surrounding urban bustle. Inside, the church is renowned for its stunning ceiling paintings depicting the 14 Stations of the Cross and other biblical scenes, all illuminated by modern chandeliers and a bright, festive color palette following recent renovations. The sacred space is anchored by a well-preserved retable featuring the patron saint, the Immaculate Conception, encased in glass, while the functioning choir loft and neatly arranged pews ensure the parish remains a vibrant, well-maintained center for Sunday worship and historical preservation.

heritage_spots.name: San Antonio de Padua Parish Church
heritage_spots.info: A Renaissance-style religious landmark characterized by a spacious, landscaped patio used for community activities and a unique, two-tiered rounded bell tower painted green. While recent renovations have modernized the interior with off-white floor tiles, open-design barred windows, and contemporary ceiling fans for ventilation, the church remains a meticulously maintained spiritual hub. The sacred space is adorned with prominent statues of the Sacred Heart of Jesus and the Immaculate Heart of Mary near the entrance, while the pillars display the Stations of the Cross and a portrait of the Mother of Perpetual Help. Despite moving away from its original Vigan tile aesthetic, the church preserves its solemnity through its well-kept altar, an accessible Adoration Chapel, and a signature stained-glass upper window that adds a touch of traditional artistry to the brightened, updated hall.

heritage_spots.name: Santulan Chapel
heritage_spots.info: The Santulan Chapel, also known as the San Vicente Ferrer Chapel, is a significant religious and community landmark in Barangay Santulan, Malabon. It is widely recognized for its vibrant celebration of the feast of its patron saint, San Vicente Ferrer, which attracts many devotees and features traditional local festivities.

heritage_spots.name: Sto. Rosario Parish
heritage_spots.info: The Sto. Rosario Parish Church in Dampalit features a unique exterior defined by a concrete, inverted "U-shaped" facade topped with a central cross and a statue of the Virgin Mary. Its structural integrity is supported by fourteen Greek or Romanian columns at each corner, while the facade is detailed with a small stone balcony, a glass-paned door, and a combination of circular and rectangular stone windows. Since its major renovation in 2008, the church has successfully blended its original historical appearance with modern materials, resulting in a beautified altar and updated sacred elements. These improvements include a restored tabernacle, a new crucifix, and enhanced stained glass, alongside modernized facilities like the parish library and administrative offices.

heritage_spots.name: Gregorio Sanciangco Shrine
heritage_spots.info: A 5.62-square-meter open historical landmark located along the main road of a residential area in Barangay Tonsuya, Malabon. The shrine features a white stone monument topped with a bust of the Filipino lawyer and economist, Gregorio Sanciangco, with a black-and-gold historical marker at the base detailing his biography. Renovated by the Sangguniang Barangay, the site is characterized by tiled flooring and surrounding greenery, serving as a compact but significant tribute to a local intellectual hero.

heritage_spots.name: Romulo Bernardo House
heritage_spots.info: The Bernardo Heritage House, located near the Malabon-Navotas River, is a well-preserved "Bahay na Bato" that tells a story of adaptation and familial legacy. Its exterior features traditional white-painted wooden walls, original transom windows, and a ground floor with cement walls and iron grills that once served as a garage for calesas. In the spacious garden, the family’s commitment to conservation is evident in a gazebo repurposed from original Capiz windows and a century-old jar transformed into a functional aquarium.

heritage_spots.name: Immaculate Heart of Mary Parish
heritage_spots.info: The Archbishop of Manila, His Eminence Jaime L. Cardinal Sin, responded to the citizens of Santolan, Maysilo, and Panghulo who had requested a parish by informing the community that he would fulfill their requests. Consequently, on November 21, 1988, they canonically established the Immaculate Heart of Mary Parish, appointing Rev. Fr. Antonio Nopasa as its first parish priest.

heritage_spots.name: Malabon Zoo, Aquarium, and Botanical Garden
heritage_spots.info: Established in 1989 by dedicated conservationist Manny Tangco, the Malabon Zoo, Aquarium, and Botanical Garden in Barangay Potrero began as a private backyard collection dating back to the late 1960s. Tangco’s lifelong passion for wildlife transformed his personal sanctuary into a public educational destination, providing a local alternative to the Manila Zoo and fostering a deep-seated love for nature among its visitors. Despite the significant financial hardships brought on by the pandemic, Tangco has demonstrated unwavering commitment to his animals, sustaining the zoo’s operations through his personal savings and family support to ensure the continued welfare of its exotic inhabitants.

malabon.tips: Try the Tricycle Heritage Tour for an easy way to see all these spots in one go.
malabon.directions_template: From {user_loc}, take a jeepney to Sangandaan, then transfer to a 'Malabon-Hulo' jeepney.

trivia.trivia: The name Tullahan River came from the variety of shellfish called “Tulya”. Old residents recalled that during the early years, tulya can be seen and harvested from the river. Tullahan river was also rich in fishes during the early years. The river used to be crystal clear and the bottom or stones in the river can be seen. Fishermen have bountiful daily catches. Aside from the rich marine life, early residents can enjoy swimming and washing clothes at the Tullahan River.

Another story about the river involves the mysterious Bato couple, or "Mag-asawang Bato" on the Tullahan River, surrounded by sirens, fairies, Kapre, Tikbalang, and other entities. According to the elders, there was a couple who were punished by a fairy because they were harsh and strict with their children. As a consequence of their actions, the fairy turned the husband and wife into stone, thus earning them the name the "stone couple.".

trivia.history: During the Philippine-American War, the river was the frontline of a bloody conflict. The fighting was particularly devastating in Malabon, where the Americans suffered 150 casualties, while Filipino forces faced a staggering loss of over 600 lives. Nearby, the clashes in Meycauayan added another 90 Filipino casualties to the toll, marking the river as a significant site of colonial resistance.

trivia.aesthetics: The facade of the San Bartolome Parish Church is defined by a grand triangular pediment supported by eight massive columns and flanked by striking three-story twin bell towers. Its historic exterior is further distinguished by semi-circular arched windows, an engraved completion year, and a jubilee main door featuring intricate wood carvings of several saints.

The interior of the San Bartolome Parish is characterized by elegant marble flooring and a majestic ceiling adorned with chandeliers and paintings of 36 Catholic saints and pivotal biblical scenes. A dedicated adoration chapel on the left houses the patron saint San Bartolome alongside numerous revered figures like San Lorenzo Ruiz and St. Padre Pio, while the church pillars display the traditional Stations of the Cross.

trivia.trivia: The "Hapsburg Eagle" on the gate is a rare architectural detail in the Philippines, signifying the owner's high social standing or "Principalia" status during the Spanish era.

Built in 1861 by Fernando Raymundo—the same year Jose Rizal was born—this historic residence is a rare example of a colonial casa hacienda likely designed by the renowned architect Luciano Oliver. Now managed by the founder's fifth-generation descendants, the house serves as a living testament to 19th-century prestige and is believed to have originally served the Augustinian order. Through a careful balance of restoration and conservation, the structure has evolved to meet modern needs while successfully preserving its deep architectural and historical links to the heritage of Malabon.

Inside, the house is a living museum of the Bernardo-Santos family, accessible via grand Narra stairs that lead to a second floor filled with 1920s antiques, a 1940s piano, and functioning vintage chandeliers. The living quarters are uniquely marked with the initials of the patriarch (RB for Romulo Bernardo) and matriarch (TS for Teodora Santos) above their respective bedroom doors. Architecturally, the home utilizes callado (fretwork) and wooden balusters below the windows for ventilation—the latter historically designed for children to watch religious processions—while the ground floor now primarily serves as storage to protect the structure’s history from the area’s occasional flooding.

trivia.info: The parish initially used the modest chapel at the foot of the Malinta Bridge as its temporary location.

navotas.info: The 'Fishing Capital', Navotas holds maritime secrets and centennial religious sites.

heritage_spots.name: San Jose de Navotas Parish
heritage_spots.info: Established in 1859, it stands as a witness to the city's transformation from a fishing village to a city.

heritage_spots.name: Navotas Fisheries Port
heritage_spots.info: While industrial, it is the historical heart of the city's identity since the 1900s.

navotas.tips: Visit during the Bangus Festival (May) to see the traditional coastal celebrations.
navotas.directions_template: From {user_loc}, take a jeepney labeled 'Agora' or 'Navotas' passing through C4 road.

valenzuela.info: The 'Vibrant City', home of Dr. Pio Valenzuela.

local_routes.wawang_pulo_to_museo: Since malapit ka lang, take a jeep bound for 'Polo' or 'Malanday'. Baba ka sa Polo Church, walking distance na lang ang Museo.
local_routes.karuhatan: Take any jeep going North (Malanday). Baba sa Gen. T. De Leon or Malanday, then transfer to a Polo-bound jeep.

heritage_spots.name: Museo ni Dr. Pio Valenzuela
heritage_spots.info: The Museo ni Dr. Pio Valenzuela is a reconstructed heritage house and museum in Barangay Pariancillo Villa that stands on the original site of the revolutionary hero's ancestral home. It serves as a historical repository and commemoration showcasing the life of Dr. Pio Valenzuela, featuring personal artifacts and documents that highlight his critical role as a co-founder of the Katipunan.

heritage_spots.name: San Diego de Alcala Church
heritage_spots.info: The San Diego de Alcala Church is a historic red-brick belfry and parish located in Polo, Valenzuela, originally established by Franciscan missionaries in 1623. While the main church was largely destroyed during World War II, the surviving four-story stone bell tower remains one of the city's oldest landmarks and a significant symbol of its Spanish colonial heritage.

heritage_spots.name: Arkong Bato Park
heritage_spots.info: Arkong Bato Park in Valenzuela City is a historic linear park centered around a 1910 stone arch that once served as the provincial boundary between Bulacan and Rizal. Today, it functions as a landscaped heritage site featuring the monument of Katipunan hero Captain Delfin Velilla and provides a safe, pedestrian-friendly space for residents and tourists to explore local history.

heritage_spots.name: Fatima University Gallery
heritage_spots.info: The Fatima University Gallery is a cultural hub located within the Valenzuela Campus of Our Lady of Fatima University, specifically on Legion of Mary Street. Recently reimagined and curated, the gallery serves as a boundless outlet for artistic expression, featuring both established and emerging Filipino artists.

heritage_spots.name: Polo Park
heritage_spots.info: Polo Park, also known as the Polo People’s Park, is a vibrant community space in Valenzuela City that serves as the modern counterpart to the historic San Diego de Alcala Church. This 2,500-square-meter plaza features a dancing fountain, landscaped gardens, and a dedicated memorial to the 159 local residents who died during World War II, making it a key destination for both relaxation and historical reflection.

heritage_spots.name: Valenzuela City People's Park
heritage_spots.info: The Valenzuela City People's Park is a 1.5-hectare urban green space located in Karuhatan, serving as the city's primary hub for outdoor recreation and community gatherings. It features modern amenities such as a dancing fountain, an aero-circle for fitness activities, and shaded picnic areas, all situated conveniently next to the Valenzuela City Hall complex.

heritage_spots.name: Valenzuela City Family Park
heritage_spots.info: A nature-centric space preserving varieties of century-old trees. The Valenzuela City Family Park is a 1.1-hectare nature-centric space in Karuhatan that preserves over 30 varieties of trees, including century-old mango and santol trees. It offers a more tranquil, shaded environment compared to the People's Park, featuring a children's playground, fitness equipment, and an amphitheater for community events.

heritage_spots.name: Valenzuela City Sports Park
heritage_spots.info: Located in Barangay Wawang Pulo, it is a premier athletic facility that features a professional-grade football field, an oval track, and multiple courts for basketball and volleyball. It serves as a major hub for local athletes and fitness enthusiasts, providing the community with a modern space for organized sports tournaments and recreational training.

heritage_spots.name: D'Cove Pavlion and Fishing Ground
heritage_spots.info: DCove PAVILION is a versatile events venue and recreational spot located along the scenic Tagalag Road in Valenzuela City. It is a popular destination for those looking to combine leisure activities with social gatherings, offering a peaceful atmosphere away from the more congested parts of the city.

heritage_spots.name: Valenzuela City Paw Park and Skate Park
heritage_spots.info: The Valenzuela City Paw Park and Skate Park is a specialized recreational area in Barangay Malinta that provides dedicated zones for both pet owners and extreme sports enthusiasts. The facility features a secure, fenced-off space with agility equipment for dogs and a modern concrete park with ramps and rails designed for skateboarding, BMX, and inline skating.

heritage_spots.name: San Roque Chapel
heritage_spots.info: The San Roque Chapel in Barangay Mabolo, Valenzuela, is a significant historical site known as the Ermita de San Roque, with roots tracing back over 300 years to a miraculous legend involving a stranded image of Saint Roch. According to local history, a heavy storm once washed the statue from Meycauayan to the mangroves of Mabolo; when residents tried to return it, the image became miraculously heavy, leading the community to believe the saint wished to stay and protect the village.

heritage_spots.name: Tagalag Fishing Village
heritage_spots.info: Known as the city's "best-kept secret", this eco-tourism zone features a 1.3-kilometer boardwalk where visitors can enjoy recreational fishing, bird watching, and sunset views. The village has transformed from a quiet pond area into a lively destination for "food crawls", offering numerous lakeside restaurants and cafes that serve fresh local catches like Tilapia and Bangus.

heritage_spots.name: Tagalag Eco Park
heritage_spots.info: As the title says, this hidden park alongside Tagalag Fishing Village is a great spot for small in town events and a great relaxation spot for tourist in Valenzuela. If you prefer to jog and have a relaxing picnic, this is definitely the place. Around hundreds of solar panels sits in this park, hence, the name Tagalag Eco Park.

heritage_spots.name: National Shrine of Our Lady of Fatima
heritage_spots.info: This major pilgrimage site is the center of Fatima devotion in the Philippines and serves as the permanent home of the National Pilgrim Image (the "EDSA Image") used during the 1986 People Power Revolution. Its unique modern architectural design features a circular layout that keeps all worshippers close to the altar, and it was declared a tourist spot as early as 1982 due to its cultural and religious significance.

heritage_spots.name: Valenzuela City Museum
heritage_spots.info: The Valenzuela City Museum is an interactive historical and industrial hub located on the ground floor of the Valenzuela City Hall complex along MacArthur Highway in Barangay Karuhatan. While Museo Valenzuela in Marulas is dedicated specifically to the life of Dr. Pio Valenzuela, this museum provides a broader narrative of the city’s transformation from the Spanish-era "Pueblo de Polo" into a modern industrial powerhouse.

heritage_spots.name: Fatima Avenue
heritage_spots.info: Recently converted into a 250-meter pedestrianized green corridor, this avenue serves as a park-like connection between the Fatima Shrine and Museo Valenzuela. It is a popular "lifestyle strip" where residents go for jogging and outdoor dining, featuring heritage-style lighting, benches, and a food bazaar that showcases local Valenzuelano businesses.

heritage_spots.name: Alvarez Park Cafe
heritage_spots.info: Located in Tagalag area, this unique "floating" cafe and restaurant offers a rustic, nautical dining experience right on the water. It is a popular destination for families and cyclists who want to enjoy a relaxing breakfast or dinner with a view of the local fishing grounds.

heritage_spots.name: Kamayan sa Palapat
heritage_spots.info: Kamayan sa Palapat is a classic Filipino family restaurant in the Tagalag Fishing Village known for its budget-friendly "boodle fight" meals and relaxing riverside kubos. It offers a nostalgic dining experience where guests can enjoy traditional favorites like bulalo and crispy pata while watching the sunset over the fishing ponds.

heritage_spots.name: Tata Celo Kainan sa Palaisdaan
heritage_spots.info: Tata Celo is a popular floating restaurant and fishing spot that features charming bamboo huts situated directly over functional fishponds. It is a favorite destination for "food crawls," offering a wide menu of fresh seafood and classic Pinoy dishes in a cozy, well-lit environment that is perfect for large family gatherings.

heritage_spots.name: Valenzuela City Boardwalk
heritage_spots.info: The Valenzuela Boardwalk in Barangay Coloong serves as a serene extension of the city's eco-tourism efforts, offering a quieter and more natural alternative to the main Tagalag section. Situated along the boundary of the Coloong fishponds, this area provides visitors with panoramic views of the water and the local migratory birds that frequent the site. The site aims to connect four towns in Valenzuela namely Wawang Pulo, Tagalag, Polo, and Coloong.

heritage_spots.name: Mang Delfin's Putong Pulo
heritage_spots.info: Mang Delfin’s Putong Pulo is Valenzuela City’s most famous culinary heirloom, a bite-sized, reddish-brown steamed rice cake traditionally paired with freshly grated coconut. While the recipe for Putong Pulo originally earned national acclaim as early as 1920, the Mang Delfin brand was officially established in 1944 by Olimpio Gutierrez and Felisisima De Guzman in the old town of Polo. The business has since been passed down through four generations and is currently managed by Delfin "Mang Delfin" Gutierrez Jr., who maintains the traditional preparation method using lansungans (bamboo steamers) and a stone corn mill to grind the rice.

valenzuela.tips: Drop by the Polo Riverwalk nearby after visiting the Museum for a quiet sunset view.

trivia.trivia: Born on July 11, 1869 and died at the age of 86 on April 6, 1956 at his home in Polo, Valenzuela. Dr. Pio Valenzuela was a Filipino physician, a prominent figure in Valenzuela and a central figure of the Philippine Revolution, best known as a member of the Katipunan’s "Triumvirate" alongside Andres Bonifacio and Emilio Jacinto. Born in Polo, Bulacan, to Francisco Valenzuela and Lorenza Alejandrino, he used his medical background and his family’s principalia status to support the secret society under the alias Dimas Ayaran. He played a pivotal role in the movement by serving as its Fiscal and managing the publication of the revolutionary newspaper Kalayaan, which was instrumental in rapidly expanding the Katipunan's membership across the country. One of his most significant historical contributions was his 1896 secret mission to Dapitan, where he disguised himself to seek the counsel of Dr. Jose Rizal regarding the start of the armed uprising. Following the revolution, Dr. Valenzuela transitioned into a prolific career in public service, becoming the first municipal president of Polo and later serving as the Governor of Bulacan from 1921 to 1925. His legacy is permanently immortalized in his hometown, which was renamed Valenzuela in 1960, and his life is commemorated at his reconstructed ancestral home in Barangay Pariancillo Villa, now a museum housing his personal memorabilia.
